exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.notes: Hands raised on a step if you can't reach 8; feet raised once 15 is easy.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Reps are per leg.

exercises.name: Plank Test
exercises.notes: Hold to failure. One set, once a month — this is the measurement, not the training.

weeks.notes: Baseline. Stop each set two reps short and see where that lands.
Nothing scheduled. Walk, stretch, or do neither.

exercises.name: Burpees
exercises.notes: Steady pace you can hold for all 8 — the last round should look like the first.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.notes: Flat out for the 20 seconds. The 40 is there to make that possible.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swings
exercises.notes: 15 swings at the top of each minute; the rest of the minute is the rest.

exercises.name: AMRAP 12
exercises.notes: One round is 10 swings, 10 push-ups, 15 air squats. Count the rounds.

exercises.name: Row 2k
exercises.notes: A repeatable test. Same machine, same damper, log the time.

exercises.name: Easy Run
exercises.notes: Conversational pace. Run, bike or row — whatever you have.

weeks.notes: Set the baseline. Everything after this is measured against it.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.notes: Add 2.5 kg once all sets reach 8.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.notes: Bodyweight until 3 × 12, then hang weight from a belt.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.notes: A fixed target of 5 — no range, so no `target_reps_max` here.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.notes: Bands or a machine count. Log what you actually did.

weeks.notes: Baseline week. Leave the weights conservative and log the ranges.
Four days off before the next block of three. Written out so Kettle counts them.
Same weights, one more rep per set where the range allows it.
Fifth set on the bench from this week on.
Peak week. Everything is at its heaviest and longest.
Deload. Keep the bar moving fast, stop well short of failure.

exercises.name: Push-ups
exercises.notes: Stop 2 reps shy of failure. Hit 15 on every set twice before moving to a harder variation.

exercises.name: Inverted Rows
exercises.notes: Under a table or a low bar. Walk your feet further out to make it harder once you own the top of the range.

exercises.name: Split Squats
exercises.notes: Reps are per leg — log the weaker side, so the number you beat next time is the honest one.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes: Raise the whole range by 5s once you hit 45s on every set.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: No weight is seeded — set yours on the first session, then add the smallest jump you own once you hit 12 on every set.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.notes: Pressed off the floor, so it needs no bench. Add weight once you hit 12 on every set.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Reps are per side.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.notes: Add time before adding weight.

exercises.name: EMOM Push-ups
exercises.notes: Every minute on the minute: 8 push-ups, then rest whatever is left of the minute. Cut the target once you stop finishing inside it.

exercises.name: AMRAP 12
exercises.notes: One round is 10 push-ups, 15 bodyweight squats, 10 inverted rows. The app times the cap and counts rounds — the movements live here in the notes, since an AMRAP has no movement list of its own.

exercises.name: Easy Cardio Cooldown
exercises.notes: Run, bike, row, walk — whatever you have. Add a distance to the config if you want that tracked too.

weeks.notes: Baseline week. Log where you actually land in each range — don’t chase the top of it yet.
Rest is where the last session turns into something. Walk if you like; nothing heavy.
Same three sessions. Aim for one more rep than you logged in week 1, on every set.
A fourth set everywhere. Keep the reps where they were rather than pushing both at once.
Heaviest week of the block. Now push the reps toward the top of each range.
Last session of the block, and a fourth finisher round. Completing it loops back to week 1 — run it again with the top of each range as your new floor.
Baseline week. Pick weights you could stop 2 reps shy of failure with, and write them into each exercise.
A day between sessions is part of the plan, not a gap in it.
The A/B order flips this week. Add the smallest jump you own to anything you hit the top of the range on.
A fourth set everywhere. Hold the weights where they are this week.
Heaviest week of the block: four sets, and add weight wherever week 3 felt easy.
Last session of the block. Completing it loops back to week 1 — run it again from the weights you finished on.

exercises.name: Sit to Stand
exercises.notes: Up from a chair and back down. Hit 12 on every set twice before the program adds a fourth.

exercises.name: Wall Push-ups
exercises.notes: Step your feet further from the wall to make it harder once you own 15 on every set.

exercises.name: Heel Raises
exercises.notes: A chair back or a counter is the support. Take a hand off it before you add reps.

exercises.name: Seated March
exercises.notes: One left and one right is two reps, so the number you log counts both legs.

exercises.name: Standing Balance
exercises.notes: Held per side. Raise the whole range by 5s once you hit 30s on every set.

exercises.name: Band Row
exercises.notes: The band is the load, so a step further back is the smallest jump you have once you hit 12 on every set.

exercises.name: Hip Hinge
exercises.notes: Hands on a chair back. Move them down the chair as the range grows.

exercises.name: Walk
exercises.notes: Fifteen minutes to start. Add a distance to the config if you want that tracked too.

weeks.notes: Baseline week. Log where you actually land in each range — the bottom of it is a real answer.

A fourth set on the strength days. Keep the reps where they were rather than pushing both at once.
Last week of the block. Now push the reps toward the top of each range.
Completing this loops back to week 1 — run it again with the top of each range as your new floor.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: No weight is seeded — set yours on the first session, then add the smallest plate pair the gym has once you hit 8 on every set.

exercises.name: Bench Press
exercises.notes: Add weight once you hit 8 on every set, not on your best one.

exercises.name: Deadlift
exercises.notes: A shorter range than the rest of the block, so the top of it arrives sooner. Add weight at 5 on every set.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.notes: The smallest jump you own is a big one here. Expect to sit at the top of the range for a while.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.notes: Log assisted reps as reps. The number you beat next time is your own either way.

exercises.name: Cooldown
exercises.notes: Bike, row, walk — whatever is free. Add a distance to the config if you want that tracked too.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat

exercises.name: Clean & Press

exercises.notes: Reps are per side.

exercises.name: Rack Carry
